instagram.label: Instagram
instagram.disclosurePlacement: First line of the caption — "(Ad)" or "#ad", never only in the bio.
instagram.notes: Lead with the surprising fact, not the brand name. Carousel: one card per checklist item works well.

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.format: Short video script + on-screen text + caption
tiktok.disclosurePlacement: Spoken or on-screen text in the first 3 seconds, AND "#ad" as the first tag — a caption-only disclosure isn't enough here.
tiktok.notes: Hook has to land before second 2. State the surprising fact as a question or a myth-bust.

x.label: X
x.disclosurePlacement: "(Ad)" at the very start of the first post in the thread.
x.notes: One sharp claim per post. Save the nuance for the linked guide.

linkedin.label: LinkedIn
linkedin.format: Text post, optionally with an image of the comparison table
linkedin.disclosurePlacement: "(Ad)" or "This post contains an affiliate link" as the first line.
linkedin.notes: Frame it as a consumer-protection insight, not a sales pitch — this audience reacts badly to hype.

youtube.label: YouTube (Shorts or long-form)
youtube.disclosurePlacement: Verbal disclosure in the video itself AND "(Ad)" at the top of the description — YouTube's own paid-promotion toggle doesn't cover affiliate links.
youtube.notes: Description should stand alone as a mini version of the guide, since many viewers only read it.

pinterest.label: Pinterest
pinterest.format: Pin image (use the comparison table or checklist as the graphic) + title + description
pinterest.hashtags: Not used — Pinterest ranks on keywords in the title/description instead
pinterest.disclosurePlacement: "(Ad)" or "Paid partnership" at the start of the description.
pinterest.notes: Titles are searched more than seen — write the title as the actual question someone would type.
